key_concepts: Elements are arranged in the periodic table by increasing atomic number
Horizontal rows are periods; vertical columns are groups or families
Group number corresponds to the number of valence electrons
Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties
Groups 1, 2, and 13–18 are representative or main group elements
Group 1 alkali metals are very reactive with one valence electron; Group 2 alkaline earth
Group 17 halogens are salt-forming nonmetals with seven valence electrons; Group 18 noble
Transition metals in Groups 3–12 are hard, malleable, ductile conductors; lanthanides and
Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile, good conductors and mostly solid at room temperat
Nonmetals are dull, brittle, poor conductors and may be solid, liquid, or gas
Metalloids along the stair-step line show metal and nonmetal properties and some are semic
More reactive metals displace less reactive metals from compounds
